title: Review of the digestion-driven predator ecology (SIEXD) on fresh seed 9: counts, twin and prey-removal fork replicate; predators are bound to one prey for life and divide by tearing across two prey, mostly frames after the prey split
summary: labkit 256^2 run of the claimed world on fresh seed 9 (defaults) and its predator-free twin (pred_on 0), plus the prey-removal fork and a fed run at 128^2 with the author's drive.py. Predators: 38 persistent splits, generation 2; prey: 62 persistent splits, generation 3; the twin is a frozen emulsion (150 prey, 0 splits, 3 moving tracks). Removing the prey at t=6000 dissolves every predator by t=6800 (49 -> 0, predator material 0.105 kept; fed: 49 -> 50). On the question of what the individual is: 83-92% of predator bodies touch a prey at every 10th frame, and 302 of 306 predator tracks that live >= 20 frames touch only one prey lineage over their lives; but only 3 of 36 persistent predator splits coincide (within 1 frame, 20 px) with a prey split: predators divide by being stretched between two prey and tearing (predsplits9.png).

observations.S: rerun/seed9/sheet.png t=0: prey material noise over the whole domain; prey droplets condense by t=500 (predator noise added at t=2000, as in the claim).
observations.I: rerun/seed9/sheet.png t=2600-12000: ~190 predator comets each on the flank of a prey droplet; partners9.json: 306 predator tracks live >= 20 frames (2000 t), touching no prey in a median 2.5% of their frames, and 302/306 touch only one prey lineage over their lives. The predator is a separate body of its own conserved material, but it is carried by one prey for its whole life.
observations.X: rerun/twin_seed9 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid and duration): 150 prey, 0 persistent splits, 3 moving tracks, against 189 prey, 62 persistent splits, 332 moving tracks with predators (rerun/seed9/metrics.json species.prey).
observations.D: rerun/seed9/metrics.json species.predator: 38 persistent splits, generation 2 (prey 62, generation 3). predsplits9.png: 8 predator splits, each a predator bridging two prey that is drawn out and tears into two comets, one on each prey; coinc9.json: 3/36 predator splits within 1 frame and 20 px of a prey split, 62/62 prey splits with a predator within 8 px.
observations.E: fork/dfork_s9.json (128^2, dfork_t 6000): predators 49 -> 42 -> 35 -> 2 -> 0 at t=6000/6200/6400/6600/6800, max c_b 1.42 -> 0.46, mean predator material 0.115 -> 0.105 (kept as bath); fork/fed_s9.json same seed: 49 -> 50 predators at t=8000.

seeds_run.result: pass: 256^2 labkit (predators 38 persistent splits gen 2, prey 62 gen 3), twin frozen (0 splits), 128^2 prey-removal fork 49 -> 0 predators in 800 t

controls_run.E: fork/dfork_s9 vs fork/fed_s9 (prey removal at t=6000, same seed)

verdicts.limitation: Each predator rides one prey for essentially its whole life (302/306 tracks touch one prey lineage), and it changes partner only when it is stretched between two prey and tears; so a predator and its prey move as a pair, and the same structure could be read as a two-material individual. Against that reading, the predator is a distinct body of a conserved material separable from the prey, its divisions are mostly not simultaneous with prey divisions (3/36 within 1 frame), and the prey persists without it (twin). Predator generation is only 2 on this seed. The fork ran at 128^2 with drive.py counts, not labkit; I did not run the fuel cut for prey E, a dt/2 or a grid variant.
